verdict.line: You lose extended pokes and skirmishes before level 6, but you claw back the lane once R (Unstoppable Force) lets you force short, decisive fights instead of trading Q for Q.

brief.thesis: Tahm Kench's Q (Tongue Lash) reaches 900 units and heals him on hit, which is 275 further than your longest tool, Q (Seismic Shard) at 625, so he can poke you for free while you're still closing distance. Every Q or auto that lands on you also builds his An Acquired Taste stacks, and at three stacks he can Devour (R, 0s cooldown) you outright for burst or to pull you out of a fight. That dynamic is why this matchup sits at 46.7% over 366 games despite Malphite's healthy 52.1% average in the lane overall — your counter isn't to out-poke him, it's to deny the stacks and pick your one big engage.

theirWindow.when: Tahm sits at 3 Acquired Taste stacks
theirWindow.what: He can instantly Devour (R, 0s cooldown) you for magic damage or to yank you out of position for a gank. Back off to max range and let a cooldown trade pass before you commit to minions or a fight.

yourWindow.when: You land R while he's out of Dive range
yourWindow.what: Unstoppable Force (1000 range, knock-up) is your only reliable way to force a fight on your terms. Land it when his W (Abyssal Dive, 21-17s cooldown) is down so he can't blink out, then chain E (Ground Slam) into W (Brutal Strikes) before he resets.

start.why: The 70.2%-picked start (47.9% over 334 games); the mana and regen let you spam Q and E to chip him from range instead of standing in his Tongue Lash poke.

boots.why: Higher-performing boots here (50.5% over 184 games) and they directly cut the bonus damage from his passive, An Acquired Taste, which rides on his autos.

core.why: Best-performing core path (57.1% over 14 games); gives you the health and AoE pressure to punish him when he leashes onto a minion wave.
Piles on armor, which directly scales your E (Ground Slam) damage, and punishes his auto-attack-based passive.
Caps out your armor stacking for E scaling and slows his attack speed so his passive stacks build slower.

situational.when: you're ahead and want to burst priority targets off your R engage
your team needs sustained AoE pressure or anti-heal in extended fights
the enemy team has heavy magic damage beyond Tahm

runes.keystoneWhy: Lets you chip Tahm from max Q range before he closes the gap with his longer Tongue Lash, since you can't win a face-to-face poke war.

summoners.why: The dominant pick here (46.7% win rate, 78.7% pick rate); Teleport lets you reset and avoid forced skirmishes in a lane you're statistically behind in, while Flash backs up your R engage or bails you out of a 3-stack Devour threat.

playing.title: Trade on cooldowns, not face-to-face
playing.detail: Poke with Q (8s cooldown, steals movement speed) and E (7s cooldown, armor-scaling magic damage plus attack speed reduction), then step back. His Q heals him on hit, so standing for a second exchange favors him.

playing.title: Track his Acquired Taste stacks
playing.detail: Every Q or auto he lands on you builds a stack; at three he can Devour (R, 0s cooldown) you for burst. Disengage before he reaches three rather than fighting through it.

playing.title: Respect the 900-range Q
playing.detail: Tongue Lash outranges your Q (625) and E (400) by a wide margin. Approach behind caster minions so he has to hit them instead of you.

playing.title: Don't feed his Thick Skin
playing.detail: His E passively stores damage taken while out of combat and converts it into a shield. Long poke exchanges just charge that shield, so keep trades short and decisive.

playing.title: Save R for a clean window
playing.detail: Land Unstoppable Force when his Abyssal Dive (21-17s cooldown) is down so he can't blink away, then follow with E into W for your full burst.

playing.title: Play for scaling, not skirmishes
playing.detail: At 46.7% over 366 games, early 1v1s favor him. Farm safely behind minions and let Sunfire Aegis and Thornmail take over by level 11-13.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, boots, summoners, and all win-rate figures are measured OP.GG data from the current patch (16.20.1) with the sample sizes noted above; the ability breakdowns, trade timing, and tactical advice are my own read on top of that data, not sourced statistics.
